static_traits.name: Zhou Wanqing
static_traits.family_status: Lives with a strict father and siblings; the family is financially strapped, with strict financial control
static_traits.social_status: Weaker sense of connection with financially better-off friends, often misses social activities due to lack of money; has one friend to confide in, but has not yet discussed the financial distress
static_traits.medical_history: No notable physical illness; no prior history of psychotherapy; no similar financial stress problems occurred before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic, high cooperation; able to self-reflect but has evident 'should' statements and catastrophizing tendencies; neutral tone; when bearing shame and powerlessness, tends to ignore emotions and endure rigidly

basic_info.main_problem: As a high school student, I feel overwhelmed and worried about my financial situation, which leads to feelings of failure and stress.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because worries about finances are affecting my academic performance and mental health.
growth_experiences: After entering high school, the client began to experience persistent financial stress: the family's finances were tight and the father strictly controlled finances, making the client frequently need to ask the parents for money and feel embarrassed; the problem worsened over time, especially when seeing friends able to afford consumption and activities the client could not afford, the sense of frustration increased.

Peer comparison experiences: when friends go out or buy new items, the client feels shame and failure from being unable to participate, gradually forming a self-narrative of 'I will always fall behind' and pessimistic expectations for the future.

Self-effort with limited effect: tried budgeting and looking for part-time work, but still found it hard to relieve financial stress and anxiety, accompanied by the high-standard internal demand 'I should handle everything well'.

Interpersonal and academic impact: avoids socializing due to financial constraints, with reduced sense of connection; financial worries intrude into study situations, causing attention and academic performance to decline.

core_beliefs: I am not as good as others

special_situations.event: Friends arrange to go out or buy new items, while oneself has to decline due to lack of money
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot spend money and participate in activities like my peers, it means I am inferior to them / I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids social activities and conceals the financial situation, pressuring the self through comparison to motivate the self to 'catch up'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am always behind; they will think I am no good

special_situations.event: Needing to ask parents for money
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I need to rely on parents, it proves I am incompetent and disappoint my family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores emotions and toughs it out without asking about needs, attempting to maintain control through self-blame and self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is my fault; I should be able to handle it myself

special_situations.event: While studying, is interrupted by financial worries and attention declines
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even do such a basic thing (focusing on study) well, then I am a complete failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-blame and doubling demands for perfect performance to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot even concentrate on studying; I am done for

special_situations.event: Repeatedly missing peers' social activities due to lack of money
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the economic situation cannot be improved now, it will not get better in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly rehearsing the worst outcome, worrying excessively in order to 'prepare in advance'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never catch up; the future will not be better either

core_conflict.wish: Longs for autonomy, competence, and peer acceptance (not being looked down on for financial straits)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and falling behind in comparisons, worrying that exposing vulnerability will lead to humiliation or negation
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control through self-harshness and high standards, avoiding being hurt by external evaluation
Maintaining independence and not seeking help to avoid the shame of dependence

object_relations.object_representation: An other who is harsh, controlling, and possibly negating of the self (such as a strict father / judgmental peers)

object_relations.self_representation: A person who must suppress needs and cannot trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: Others who are unwilling to provide support or who would judge oneself for it

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites delving into emotional experiences such as shame/failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Expressing vulnerability will lead to being judged or controlled (projecting the father's harsh image onto the counselor)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in analytical and strategic language, emphasizing the 'how to' of budgets and part-time work, avoiding concrete emotional feelings; restrained, objective tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to try changing thinking or to do practice, but worrying about not doing well
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If it is not done well, one will be negated; failure is blamed on oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses self-blaming expressions (such as 'it is all because I am incapable / I should be better'), slows speech rate and lowers volume, downplaying discussion of external factors.

manifestations: Longs for financial independence and self-direction, but is constrained by family financial straits and a strict father
Bound by the condition of worth that 'everything should be handled well', lacking tolerance for imperfection
outcomes: A rigid pattern of maintaining control through self-reproach

manifestations: Difficulty connecting with more affluent peers, often excluded from social circles
Although there is a close friend, financial troubles have not been discussed, and channels of emotional support are limited
outcomes: Worsening shame and sense of inferiority
Avoiding socializing, increased comparison and despair

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently uses 'should / must': such as 'as a high school student I should not be this poor' and 'I should handle everything well'
Judging self-worth by external comparison standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Personalizing the predicament as 'it is all my fault; I am incapable'
Expressing needs cautiously in sessions, worried about being judged

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Ignores and suppresses emotions such as shame / powerlessness, choosing to 'tough it out / push through'
Does not express financial difficulties and support needs to friends or family

positive_force: Willing to try identifying and questioning negative thoughts (open attitude toward change)
Having certain skills and past experience of coping with challenges
Having tried budgeting and part-time work, having capacity for action and sense of responsibility
Having a friend one can confide in, having potential social support
Able to briefly gain a more balanced perspective with evidence support (self-awareness ability)
negative_force: Marked cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, personalization, and 'should' statements
Upward comparison with peers reinforces shame and inferiority, forming a 'laggard' self-identity
Family financial straits and the internalization of control / evaluation from a strict father reduce the sense of autonomy
Avoiding socializing to escape shame, leading to isolation and reinforcement of negative self-narrative
Negative predictions about the future and a low sense of control trigger persistent anxiety, interfering with academic focus

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent excessive worry about money and catastrophic self-talk
antecedent: When friends arrange to go out or buy new things
When needing to ask parents for money
When thinking about financial burdens and expenses during study
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized belief 'I am a failure' and a cognitive pattern of extrapolating current financial straits into a lifetime of failure
target_behavior.function: Seeking a sense of control and preventing failure through excessive vigilance and self-blame
target_behavior.consequence: Increased anxiety and stress, decreased attention, impaired academic performance

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social activities out of worry about embarrassment and being judged
antecedent: Friends initiate social activities that require spending money
Peers show off new purchases or spending plans
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing exposing financial straits will be looked down on by others, accompanied by shame and inferiority
target_behavior.consequence: Distanced from peers; feelings of loneliness and 'falling behind' are reinforced

target_behavior.behavior: Self-blaming 'should' self-talk and toughing it out while ignoring emotions
antecedent: When academic performance is affected and self-rated as 'failure'
target_behavior.core_reason: Conditions of worth with high standards internalized from a strict father and external comparisons (introjection)
target_behavior.function: Maintaining order and control through self-blame, avoiding the shame of seeking help externally
target_behavior.consequence: Accumulated stress and emotional exhaustion, decreased motivation to change, problem cycle continues
